description: Weaver Usenet downloader: throughput, pipeline backpressure, per-server health, and post-processing.

panels.description: Bytes per second pulled from Usenet, measured as the rate of the download counter rather than the smoothed speed gauge.
panels.title: Download speed

panels.description: Bytes downloaded in the last 24 hours. Compare against your download quota.
panels.title: Downloaded / 24h

panels.description: Article segments waiting to be fetched. Recovery work is included; subtract weaver_pipeline_recovery_queue_depth for required-only depth.
panels.title: Queue depth

panels.description: Jobs by status. Statuses with no jobs report 0, so the series set is stable.
panels.title: Jobs by status

panels.description: What is currently limiting the downloader. Exactly one limiter is 1 at any moment.
panels.title: Observed limiter

panels.description: Backpressure state and the gate reason blocking downloads, if any.
panels.title: Pressure and gate

panels.description: Bytes held in the decode and write stages against their soft pressure limits.
panels.title: Decode and write backlog

panels.description: Download lanes by scheduler state. Lanes stuck in awaiting_work or parking mean the scheduler cannot feed them.
panels.title: Download lanes by state

panels.description: Per-server health state. Anything other than healthy is worth a look; the reason is on weaver_server_state_reason.
panels.title: Server state

panels.description: Connection permits still free versus the runtime maximum. A flat zero means the servers, not the pipeline, are the bottleneck.
panels.title: Connections available vs max

panels.description: EWMA request latency per server.
panels.title: Server latency

panels.description: BODY bytes per second from each server. Shows which provider is actually carrying the job.
panels.title: Per-server throughput

panels.description: Fraction of each server's configured download quota consumed in the current window.
panels.title: Server quota used

panels.description: Share of article fetches each server answered with 'article not found'. The clearest provider-retention signal there is: a climbing miss ratio means that server is losing articles, even while it still looks healthy.
panels.title: Article miss ratio per server

panels.description: 95th percentile article fetch latency per server.
panels.title: Article latency p95 per server

panels.description: Jobs reaching a terminal state, by result. A rising 'failed' share is the headline reliability number.
panels.title: Jobs finished by result

panels.description: 95th percentile wall-clock time jobs spent in each pipeline stage. Shows where the time actually goes.
panels.title: Stage duration p95

panels.description: Post-processing scripts waiting and running.
panels.title: Post-processing queue

panels.description: Completed post-processing attempts per second, by outcome.
panels.title: Post-processing results

panels.description: Archive entries refused by the extraction guardrails. A sustained non-zero rate usually means a malformed or hostile archive, not a Weaver bug.
panels.title: Extraction rejections

panels.description: Verify, repair, and extract workers busy right now, plus disk write latency.
panels.title: Post-download workers

panels.description: Resident and virtual memory of the Weaver process. Some platforms cannot report these cheaply, in which case the series are absent rather than zero.
panels.title: Process memory

panels.description: CPU cores consumed by the Weaver process, plus thread and file-descriptor counts.
panels.title: Process CPU, threads and fds

panels.description: Each script's last run: status, duration and age, with its run rate and failure ratio over the last hour. Failures count failed, timed_out, not_started and interrupted runs.
panels.title: Script status

panels.description: Run duration quantiles per script across every run kind.
panels.title: Script duration p50 / p95

panels.description: Finished script runs per second, stacked by status.
panels.title: Script runs by status

panels.description: Script runs holding a slot, by run kind, against the configured concurrency limit.
panels.title: Running vs limit

panels.description: Script runs waiting for a slot now, and the rate runs enter a wait, by run kind.
panels.title: Waiting for slot

panels.description: Queue events recorded for scripts and not yet started.
panels.title: Queue-event backlog

panels.description: Jobs whose post-processing pass finished, by summary.
panels.title: Job summaries

panels.description: Script runs whose captured output was truncated, per script.
panels.title: Output truncations

panels.description: Each configured rule: whether it is enabled, its last outcome, time since it last fired and its fires over the last day.
panels.title: Schedule rules

panels.description: Schedule actions applied per second, by action kind and outcome.
panels.title: Schedule actions by kind

panels.description: Why the schedule holds download admission; none means no hold.
panels.title: Admission hold

panels.description: Schedule actions replayed, by reason, and wall-clock jumps the evaluators detected.
panels.title: Replays and clock jumps

panels.description: Each route leg: state, time since a scrape first saw it, connections, throughput and the ladder rung its last connection used.
panels.title: Route legs

panels.description: Each egress: health, time since a scrape first saw it, leg dial failures and cooldowns over the last hour, and download rate.
panels.title: Egresses

panels.description: Session preparations per second on session-based proxy hops, and the share that failed, by proxy kind.
panels.title: Proxy session handshakes

panels.description: Streams opened through proxy hops per second, and the share that failed, by proxy kind.
panels.title: Proxy streams

panels.description: Members of each proxy pool stage: total, warmed and blocked.
panels.title: Pool stage sizes

panels.description: Share of host name lookups for routed connections that failed, by resolver.
panels.title: DNS failure ratio

panels.description: Route stages revoked, and connections made past a ladder's first rung, by rung.
panels.title: Revocations and ladder fallbacks

panels.description: Bytes per second each route leg carried.
panels.title: Leg throughput

title: Weaver — Overview
